newsitem.title: USA: Dime says $15 mln charge in Q2 to be offset.
newsitem.headline: Dime says $15 mln charge in Q2 to be offset.

text.p: Dime Bancorp Inc said Tuesady that it reached agreements during the second quarter of 1997 to sell approximately $126 million of its non-performing residential loans and owned real estate.

The bank said it estimates that these sales will result in a one-time pre-tax charge in the second quarter of approximately $15 million. But it said the loss is expected to be substantially offset by reinvestment earnings and lower credit-related costs during the balance of the year.
Adjusted for the sales, on a pro forma basis as of March 31, 1997, Dime said its portfolio of non-performing assets would be approximately $104 million, or 0.57 percent of total assets.
The planned transactions are, said Dime, still subject to standard closing conditions, and no assurance can be given that they will be consummated as anticipated.

In other news, the bank also said its proposed acquisition of BFS Bankorp Inc has received all required approvals and is scheduled to close in the second quarter of 1997. Completion of the acquisition will add approximately $600 million of loans and $450 million of deposits to Dime's balance sheet.
At March 31 Dime had assets of $18.5 billion, deposits of $12.8 billion, and stockholders' equity of $1.1 billion.
